claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Mphasis (NSE: MPHASIS) sells IT services to clients in banking and financial services, insurance, technology, media and telecom, and logistics and transportation; its consolidated revenue in FY26 was ₹15,880 crore.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: In the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹4,581 crore, 17.4% more than a year earlier; the operating margin was 14.7% against 15.2%, and profit attributable to shareholders was ₹561 crore, 19.6% higher.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: On 6 Nov 2026, the first session after the result, MPHASIS shares rose 0.40% while the NIFTY 50 rose 2.01% and the NIFTY IT index rose 0.43%; allowing for the market's move, MPHASIS's own move was -1.29%, about 0.74 times its usual daily variation.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: These numbers measure the move, not its cause: the result, the IT sector's rise and any other news that day overlap, and nothing here separates them.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: At ₹2,468 (NSE close, 23 Nov 2026), the reinvestment-phase discounted cash flow model (Template B, since MPHASIS's median return on invested capital of 23.4% is above its 11.92% cost of capital) matches the price if revenue grows about 23.9% a year for five years at the FY26 operating margin of 15.3%; MPHASIS's revenue grew 4.8% a year over FY23–FY26.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: With the other assumptions at base, the valuation is most sensitive to the cost of capital (one percentage point either way: a model value of ₹949 to ₹1,287 a share) and to the operating margin (two percentage points either way: a model value of ₹942 to ₹1,244 a share); the Q3 FY27 result will be the next reported quarter.

prices.note: Each series is rebased to 100 on the first common session. Raw exchange prices are not published here (NSE terms).

metrics.label: Market cap
metrics.definition: Price × shares outstanding (share capital ÷ ₹10 face value at 2026-09-30).

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.definition: Price ÷ earnings per share over the last four reported quarters (Q3 FY26 – Q2 FY27).

metrics.label: EV / EBIT (TTM)
metrics.definition: Enterprise value (market cap − the net cash and treasury figure below) ÷ operating profit over the last four quarters.

metrics.label: Net cash and treasury
metrics.definition: Cash, bank balances and treasury investments, plus investments in joint ventures and associates, less lease liabilities, borrowings, preference shares and minority interests, at 30 Sep 2026.

metrics.label: Operating margin (FY26)
metrics.definition: EBIT ÷ revenue, after depreciation, excluding other income. Sites that quote an EBITDA-based margin show a higher figure.

metrics.label: ROE (FY26)
metrics.definition: Profit for the year ÷ total equity at year end.

metrics.label: ROIC (FY26)
metrics.definition: After-tax EBIT ÷ invested capital at the start of the year. Invested capital excludes about ₹4k crore of cash and treasury.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY23–FY26
metrics.definition: Compound annual growth of revenue from FY23 to FY26.

metrics.label: Cash conversion (FY26)
metrics.definition: Operating cash flow ÷ profit for the year.

metrics.label: Beta vs NIFTY 50
metrics.definition: Sensitivity of MPHASIS's daily return to the NIFTY 50's, over the two years to the price date.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.what: Revenue grows at 50% of its FY23-FY26 rate for five years, the operating margin slips 2 points, and growth after year 10 earns no more than its cost of capital.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.what: Revenue keeps its FY23-FY26 growth rate for five years, the FY26 margin holds, and MPHASIS keeps its historical return on capital indefinitely.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.what: Revenue grows 2 points a year faster than its FY23-FY26 rate for five years and the margin rises 1 point.

valuation.rule_note: The cost of debt and long-run growth are set by fixed rules and not reviewed by a person.

template_b.name: Template B · reinvestment phase
template_b.why: Template A needs free cash flow to the firm to be positive in at least three of the last four years, and here it was ₹415 crore in FY24, ₹1,218 crore in FY25 and −₹380 crore in FY26.
template_b.test: Template B runs the same model but asks a different question of the past: does the capital being reinvested earn more than it costs? The median return on invested capital over FY24–FY26 was 23.4%, against a cost of capital of 11.92%. Its bear and bull cases are set around the history growth rate, because the latest years are the reinvestment itself.
tiles: economic profit after year 10, today's value
template_b.first_positive: In the base case, free cash flow turns positive in FY27: until then the growth is paid for by reinvestment, while economic profit is already positive.

flags.title: The reinvestment version of the model is used
flags.text: Template A did not apply (free cash flow not positive in at least 3 of the last 4 years), so this page uses Template B, which is judged on return on capital and assumes today's return on capital lasts.

flags.title: The exchange's files contain errors
flags.text: 9 reconciliation checks fail on the exchange's own files, each with a recorded reason. They are marked as explained, not passed, and the figure as filed is used, never a corrected one.

flags.title: One balance sheet is missing its lease lines
flags.text: The lease lines at 30 September 2025 could not be read: the statement pages of that results document are images with no text. That date is not one of the balance sheets the valuation uses; the latest one (30 September 2026) is complete.

limitations: Template B (reinvestment phase): the same single-stage fade model, judged on return on capital rather than past free cash flow. The base case assumes today's return on capital lasts; no currency driver.
Cash flows are discounted to the balance-sheet date, 30 Sep 2026, two months before the price date; the model does not roll that gap forward, so its values are slightly low against the price.
Debt is borrowings plus lease liabilities; earmarked bank balances are counted as cash, which overstates cash slightly.
The risk-free rate is a twelve-month average while the price and equity risk premium are point-in-time.
The event study measures the size of a move, not its cause; five results days are too few for statistical claims.
Free cash flow was negative in FY26, so the reinvestment template (B) applies rather than template A; its base case assumes the current return on capital lasts.
Mphasis' results are printed in INR million; lines taken from its results PDFs are converted to INR crore by the engine.

Before March 2026 the XBRL files fold lease liabilities into other financial liabilities; the lease lines for March 2022 to March 2025 come from the results PDFs. The lease lines at 30 September 2025 are missing: the statement pages of that results PDF are images with no text layer and could not be read here.
Mphasis files its share of the result of equity-accounted investees as a line inside other expenses, so that small amount sits inside operating profit as the engine computes it.

From December 2025 the XBRL files put other comprehensive income on the line for the owners' total comprehensive income; the error is listed, not corrected, in the reconciliation report, and that line is not used.
Static page: prices are end-of-day as of the date shown, not live.
